format_rules.rule: The SCOS-2000 Mission Information Base has a static part (the 'database' imported from the ASCII tables) and a dynamic part (the packet archive). Each ASCII file holds exactly one table, so 'ASCII file' and 'ASCII table' are used interchangeably.

A raw value is a parameter value before calibration (monitoring) or after de-calibration (commanding); the engineering value is the calibrated value. The raw value is not the encoded bit pattern on the link: SCOS-2000 decodes/encodes according to the type, and the two coincide only for unsigned integers (e.g. raw -1 in a 16-bit signed integer is encoded as 0xFFFF). Encoded values are never displayed.
'Name' denotes an alphanumeric unique ID (typically up to 8 characters, e.g. a parameter or calibration); 'identifier' denotes a numeric unique ID (e.g. a verification stage).

The ICD covers only the generic part of the static database used by SCOS-2000 functions; missions may add mission-specific extensions. MIB data are exported from the mission's off-line database system into ASCII files, placed in a directory read by the importer, imported into the run-time database, and used once the consuming applications restart.

Each table is delivered as one file named after the table in lower case with the extension .dat (e.g. pcf.dat). Lower case is required because the operating system is case sensitive; table acronyms in the text may appear in either case.
format_rules.history: Same rule in issue 5.1 (PDF p.12 of icd-5-1-tos-gci).

format_rules.rule: Each dynamic synthetic parameter (OL, PCF_NATUR='D'; SPEL, PCF_NATUR='P') is defined in its own file whose name is the parameter name (PCF_NAME) with no extension. OL files live in the directory given by the MISCconfig variable IMPT_EXPR_DIR, SPEL files in IMPT_SPEL_DIR. A file may contain any number of lines; the importer reads and verifies its content.
format_rules.history: Issue 5.1 named a typical location /home/sops1/data/ASCII/SYNTHETIC for these files (PDF p.12 of icd-5-1-tos-gci).

format_rules.rule: SCOS-2000 can control several 'domains'. Each domain has its own set of ASCII files (including synthetic parameter files) in a configurable directory, with sub-directories for synthetic parameter expressions. The General Domain additionally uses a 'multi-domain database' that only contains multi-domain synthetic parameters.
format_rules.history: Issue 5.1 described a single directory (typically /home/sops1/data/ASCII) without domains (PDF p.12 of icd-5-1-tos-gci).

format_rules.rule: Files are in Unix format (LF line ends) and contain one line per table record; all records of a file share the same structure.
format_rules.history: The explicit 'Unix format' statement was added in issue 7.0 (S2K-7551, Annex 2, PDF p.262).

format_rules.rule: The field separator is the tabulation (TAB) character. Every field must be present at least as its separator, i.e. an empty field consists of the TAB alone. A mission may choose another separator, which must then be configured in the importer.
format_rules.history: Issue 5.1 stated only that the separator is a TAB (PDF p.12 of icd-5-1-tos-gci); the 'at least the separator' wording is present in 6.7 Draft A (PDF p.20) and 6.9 (PDF p.22).

format_rules.rule: Mission-specific fields not defined by the ICD must be appended after the last ICD field of the table. Their length is limited only by the maximum string size of the importer host.
The end-of-file convention is EOF (no special terminator record).

Some tables have no position field, so the off-line system must deliver their records already sorted where the ICD requests it; e.g. VPD sorted by VPD_TPSD and VPD_POS, GPC by GPC_NUMBE and GPC_POS, SPC by SPC_NUMBE and SPC_POS, and OCP checks are applied in import order (sorted by OCP_NAME and OCP_POS).

Field types are Number (integers only, signed or unsigned) or Char. Char fields may contain ASCII letters A-Z and digits 0-9 plus underscore, plus/minus, dot and dash; other ASCII characters should be avoided. A field's content can be further constrained by its nature, e.g. parameter values must follow the type-specific formats of Appendix A.

Declared lengths such as Char(8) or Number(5) are maxima; shorter values are allowed. If the allowed range is narrower than the length implies, the field description says so. Fields without a declared length have a variable maximum that depends on another limit, as for command parameter values whose size depends on the maximum command size.
format_rules.history: The sentence about fields without a declared length is new in issue 7.0 (S2K-8073, Annex 2, PDF p.261).

format_rules.rule: Spaces in names (unique IDs of database items) are discouraged. Names must be unique regardless of letter case (A1000 and a1000 may not coexist); the importer gives no warning about such clashes.

Monitoring parameter names may not begin with 'VAR', 'GVAR' or '$', because the Operations Language recognises these prefixes. The patterns NNOiiii, CEBiiii, KRUiiii, MSPiiii, VL2iiii, PERiiii, REDiiii and MLGiiii (iiii = 0000-9999) are reserved for ground-station telemetry.
format_rules.history: The '$' restriction was introduced by DCR-261 (issue 5.1 Annex 1, PDF p.119 of icd-5-1-tos-gci); the ground-station reserved names were added in 7.0 (S2K-6884, PDF p.262).

format_rules.rule: A field position followed by '*' marks a key field: a table may contain only one record per combination of key values (e.g. plf is keyed on PLF_NAME and PLF_SPID, so a parameter may appear only once per packet). A position followed by '+' (e.g. '3+' for TPCF_SIZE) continues a description split across pages.

A field row with grey background is not used by SCOS-2000 processing (kept for off-line consistency checking or for historical reasons). Italic text or rows denote options/fields not yet supported. A table shaded grey as a whole is not imported; it only suggests a structure for mission-specific applications.
Floating-point values are written in decimal. Integer values may be written in decimal, hexadecimal or octal following the C++ convention: 0x12F4 is hexadecimal, 0767 octal and 767 decimal.
format_rules.history: Issue 5.1 required all numeric values in decimal unless a field said otherwise (PDF p.20 of icd-5-1-tos-gci); the C++ convention appears in 6.7 Draft A (PDF p.34) and 6.9 (PDF p.36).

format_rules.rule: An 'M' in the last column marks a mandatory field that may not be empty. All key fields are marked mandatory, even when shaded grey.
Optional fields may be left empty, in which case only the separator appears for that field.

The value in the last column (e.g. 'N', '0') is the default the importer applies when an optional field is empty; optional fields without such a default are imported as null. This import default is unrelated to default values that off-line editors may propose.

Issue 7.0 changes are designed to be backward compatible: tables and fields added since the previous issue may be omitted and modified fields may be filled as described in the previous issue (newer options such as delta checks are then simply not available).
PCF fields 20-23 (PCF_CORR, PCF_OBTID, PCF_DARC, PCF_ENDIAN) are optional for backward compatibility: the importer accepts PCF records with 19, 20, 21, 22 or 23 fields.

vdf.dat is mandatory and must contain at least one record. If it has several records, the last one imported sets the internal database version name and description; the name is used for display and to check that e.g. a saved stack file is loaded with the same database version. A null VDF_DOMAINID means the local domain; null VDF_RELEASE/VDF_ISSUE mean 0. The importer cross-checks the domain identifier against its command-line option.
All tables are normalised: each field holds a single entity, never a list, and many-to-many relationships are expressed through mapping tables (e.g. CVP, PSM, CDF, GRPA).
Identifiers of numerical (CAF_NUMBR), polynomial (MCF_IDENT) and logarithmic (LGF_IDENT) calibrations share one namespace and must not overlap, e.g. by a naming convention or reserved ranges.

Only parameters processed by the telemetry model (those defined in PLF, or synthetic parameters) may be used for CDF_TMID, CUR_RLCHK, PCF_VALID, OCP_RLCHK, PTV_PARNAM, CVE_PARNAM and in monitoring displays; values from variable packets can only be shown by the VPD application.
Command elements are encoded back to back with no gaps, so every part of the raw command packet, including padding or unused bits, must be defined as an element in CDF.

The maximum command size is set by the MISC variable CMDP_MAX_BLOCK_SIZE (default 248 bytes). Parameter space is reduced by the packet header (sum of PCDF_LEN), the CRC (CMD_CRC_SIZE, default 2 bytes) and, for time-tagged commands, the TC(11,4) wrapper named by CMD_LOAD_TT_NAME (20 bytes if that command is not found). Example given: 248 bytes with a 10-byte header and no CRC or time tag leaves 238 bytes for one parameter.
format_rules.history: Added in issue 7.0 (S2K-8073 and S2K-8063, Annex 2, PDF p.261-262).

format_rules.rule: Each file is checked against the field characteristics in the ICD; anomalies produce warnings (when the relevant import flag is set) and all messages are written to a log file overwritten at every import (/home/sops1/Import.log). The checks catch only the most dangerous inconsistencies; overall consistency is the responsibility of the off-line database system, and an off-line consistency checker is delivered with the SCOS-2000 test environment from R4.0.
format_rules.history: Issue 5.1 instead pointed to an example of consistency checks in its RD-4 (PDF p.13 of icd-5-1-tos-gci).

format_rules.rule: A value longer than its declared field length is truncated with a warning; the truncation can affect later processing unless the field is a display-only description.
An empty mandatory field triggers a warning and is imported as 0 for numbers or an empty string for strings; this situation should never occur.
Referential integrity between tables is checked: a record that refers to a missing item (e.g. an undefined parameter) is not imported and a warning is issued.

Command and sequence parameter values are syntax-checked against the format of their type (Appendix A). Invalid values produce a warning and are replaced by 0 (integers, reals, delta times), an empty string (ASCII strings) or 1970.001.00.00.00 (absolute times).

The importer supports a full import (default; creates a new internal database, optionally for a given domain; from the General Domain any domain including the multi-domain database can be imported) and a 'check only' mode that reports table-structure and field-length check results without changing data.
format_rules.history: Issue 5.1 also offered 'monitoring tables only', 'commanding tables only' and 'selected tables only' imports (PDF p.13 of icd-5-1-tos-gci); these partial options were removed because the evolution line does not support them (7.0 Annex 1 item 1, PDF p.244).

format_rules.rule: From SCOS-2000 R5.0, command sequence (csf, css, sdf, csp) and display (dpf, dpc, gpf, gpc, spf, spc) definitions are not loaded into the POST run-time database: on user request they are converted into XML files stored in the FARC (formats in AD-4 and AD-5), imported independently of the TM/TC database and on a 'delta' basis (only the delivered definitions are updated; existing ones are kept).

With the SCOS-2000 packetiser, PLF bit/byte offsets of fixed packets count from the start of the TM source packet header, while VPD positions count from the beginning of the TM source packet header plus the number of bytes given in PID_DFHSIZE (typically the source packet header plus the data field header).

time_formats.detail: PFC 0: CUC/CDS with P-field (not supported). PFC 1: CDS without microseconds, 6 octets without P-field (from R5.0). PFC 2: CDS with microseconds, 8 octets without P-field (command parameters only). PFC 3-18: CUC without P-field, coarse time 1-4 octets and fine time 0-3 octets, total octets = coarse + fine, where coarse = 1 + floor((PFC-3)/4) and fine = (PFC-3) mod 4. PFC 30: Unix time, 4 octets of seconds since 1970-01-01 00:00:00 plus 4 octets of microseconds (not a PUS type). Time code definitions are referred to CCSDS 301.0-B-2 (RD-8).
PFC 3-18: relative time in CUC layout with the same coarse/fine octet mapping as PTC 9 (1 to 7 octets in total). No CDS or P-field variants are listed for relative times.
SCOS-2000 does not recognise the time format from a P-field; the time type must be known implicitly and declared in the TM/TC database.

Absolute times are written yyyy.ddd.hh.mm.ss (day of year), e.g. 2001.159.23.59.59; relative times +/-[ddd.]hh.mm.ss[.mmm], e.g. -00.01.00 or +251.23.59.59.010. Conversion to the on-board encoding uses a mission-specific time correlation routine. Time parameters cannot be calibrated.
A command/sequence absolute-time value that fails the syntax check is replaced by 1970.001.00.00.00 (delta times by 0) with a warning.

PCF_CORR / CPC_CORR (default 'Y') select whether absolute time parameters are converted with the time correlation; they must be 'N' for relative times. PCF_OBTID / CPC_OBTID select which on-board clock (OBT ID 1..N) provides the time format and correlation; if empty, the default OBT ID from MISCconfig TCO_DEFAULT_OBT_ID is used. Without correlation and without OBT ID the epoch is given by MISCconfig TCO_ESA_EPOCH.
time_formats.history: Fields added in issue 6.7 for R5.2 (S2K-SCR-4917, PDF p.258); issue 6.9 states the OBT ID fields apply from s2k52 (S2K-DCR-5743, PDF p.260); 7.0 clarified that CORR must be 'N' for relative times (S2K-8572, S2K-8778, PDF p.262-263).

time_formats.topic: packet time and parameter time offsets
time_formats.detail: PID_TIME flags whether the TM source packet carries a packet generation time field; PID_INTER gives the generation interval of periodic packets in milliseconds (used for expiry). PLF_TIME is the time offset of the first occurrence of a parameter relative to the packet time in ms (range -4080000 to 4080000) and PLF_TDOCC the delay between super-commutated occurrences in ms (1 to 4080000, default 1).

CSS_RELTIME (delta release time) is written hh.mm.ss, at most 23.59.59; CSS_EXTIME (delta execution time-tag) is written [+][ddd.]hh.mm.ss[.mmm] for positive and -[ddd.]hh.mm.ss[.mmm] for negative intervals.

Execution time-tagged commands are encapsulated in a TC(11,4) command that must exist in CCF and CDF; its name and parameters are configured by MISCconfig CMD_LOAD_TT* variables. Only absolute time tags are supported for Service 11, not relative ones.

Service 9 time reports are used by the SCOS-2000 time correlation to build time couples (OBT and corresponding UTC), supporting free-running and synchronised clocks from R5.2; earlier releases treated time correlation as mission specific.

Issue 5.1 listed 9/1 (CDS without microseconds) as not supported and had no 9/30 (Unix) row; 9/1 became supported in R5.0 (issue 6.4, 7.0 Annex 1 PDF p.254) and 9/30 was added in issue 6.7 (PDF p.258 of icd-7-0-final).

Queried tables pcf and cpc of MIB__20250916M25925PFMS001_SOL: monitoring parameters use 9/15 (2116, CUC 4+0), 9/17 (1677, CUC 4+2), 9/30 (2), 9/2 (1), 10/6 (6), 10/15 (4) and 10/17 (37); command parameters use 9/15 (35), 9/17 (23) and 10/17 (1). PCF_CORR is empty (import default 'Y') for the CUC absolute times and 'N' for all relative times and for the 9/2 and 9/30 parameters; PCF_OBTID and CPC_OBTID are empty for all time parameters.

change_log.summary: Clarifications plus R4.0 extensions. Annex 1: PCF_PID and PID_SPID ranges raised to 2^32-1 (DCR-2421); super-commutated parameters in ANDs (DCR-2422); Herschel/Planck check-out repatriation: conditional calibration selection (CUR), delta limits, enable/inhibit of parameters, packets and groups (GRP/GRPA/GRPK), calibration curve IDs from NUM(4) to CHAR(10), CVS ID from NUM(5) to NUM(8), range set IDs from NUM(4) to CHAR(10), logarithmic calibration (LGF), editable string parameters on manual stacks, optional automatic insertion of the PUS length of variable strings; Cryosat repatriation: Command ID and Parameter ID parameter types and default sub-schedule IDs in CCF/CSF; R4.0: VDF domain/release/issue fields, GPC domain field, multiple OOL sets for status parameters, free text entries in ANDs, dynamic disabling of report verification (CCF_ACK); EGSE only: PCF_NATUR 'P' for SPEL parameters.

Additional clarifications: 5/4 reals limited to command parameters (DCR-808); CVS_SOURCE/CVS_TYPE descriptions, progress reports only at stage 0 (DCR-0821); PLF_TDOCC default is 1, 0 not allowed (DCR-847); integration of P_S2K3.1-M03/M04 DCRs (CSF_IFTT option B text); PID_PI1_VAL/PI2_VAL descriptions (CRY-OG-655); CDF_VALUE clarifications (no fixed areas for Service 11 modelled elements, group repeater may be 0); delta check values in OCP; TPCF_SIZE depends on the SCOS-2000 packet header version; SPPG multi-domain configuration (DCR-844).

PCF_USCON description updated (S2K-DCR-2984) and integration of S2K-3.1 M02-M04 updates: PCF_VALID, PCF_INTER, PCF_SPTYPE descriptions; PCF_NATUR mandatory flag removed; field types/descriptions of CAF_NUMBR, CAP_NUMBR, TXF_NUMBR, TXP_NUMBR, CVS_ID, CVP_CVSID, CCA_NUMBR changed; VPD_FORM, CPC_INTER, CDF_INTER, CDF_VALUE, SDF_VALSET, PVS_INTER, CCA_DESCR updated.
Added to Annex 1 the indication of the document updates that were missing in issue 6.2.

TC sequence and TM display definitions moved out of the POST MIB database into the FARC as XML files (sections 2.5, 3.3.2.7, 3.3.3.3; AD-4/AD-5); SLE Throw Event command type in CCF_CTYPE; command parameters of type Deduced; time type 9/1 supported. Clarifications for all releases: only TM-model parameters usable for CDF_TMID, CUR_RLCHK, PCF_VALID, OCP_RLCHK, PTV_PARNAM, CVE_PARNAM and displays; limit checks always in pairs; checks of any severity may stand alone; SDF only for editable parameters; packetiser recognises packets without data field header; ways to force the width of deduced parameters.

R4.2: optional PIC_APID to define PI1/PI2 per APID/type/subtype (SPR-3071, DCR-4535); SDF_REPPOS for commands with group repeaters in sequences (SPR-2904). R5.0: NIS Throw Events (two Throw Event types: SLE provider and NIS); CSP_FPNUM range to 65535; several packets per SPID deprecated. Clarifications: BEHV_ENABLE_OPTIMIZATION requires MVC_MAX_CONST_NUMBR above the largest OCF_NBCHCK; Table 5 variable string description corrected; long field descriptions split (TPCF_SIZE, CCF_CTYPE, CSS_RELTIME, CSS_EXTIME, SDF_VTYPE); use of pid.dat fields (DCR-3398).

notes.text: Primary source: SCOS-2000 Database Import ICD EGOS-MCS-S2K-ICD-0001 issue 7.0 FINAL (2017-08-11), slug icd-7-0-final (copied 2026-11-05T13:53:46Z from solarorbiter.irap.omp.eu). History from issue 6.9 (icd-6-9-archive-org, copied 2026-11-05T13:53:56Z), 6.7 Draft A (icd-6-7-drafta, 2026-11-05T13:53:58Z) and S2K-MCS-ICD-0001-TOS-GCI issue 5.1 (icd-5-1-tos-gci, 2026-11-05T13:54:02Z). Data statistics from Solar Orbiter MIB releases MIB__20250916M25925PFMS001_SOL (mib-20250916m25925pfms001-sol), MIB__20200416M10720PFMS001_SOL (mib-20200416m10720pfms001-sol) and the SWA instrument database (swa-idb-ascii).

All pdf_page values are PDF page indices. Printed page N corresponds to PDF page N+14 in issue 7.0, N+13 in 6.9 and 6.7 Draft A, and N+8 in 5.1 (e.g. Appendix A starts on printed page 200 = PDF p.214 in 7.0).

The lists unused_fields_grey_icd70 and unsupported_fields_italic_icd70 were derived by this project from the PDF rendering (grey fills of 85% / 75% / 80% grey behind field rows and italic fonts, extracted with mutool), not from the text. They match the ICD conventions of PDF p.35-36 but may miss or misplace rows; treat them as an aid and check the PDF page. Whole tables shaded grey: ppf, ppc (also italic) and cps.

ICD 7.0 defines 53 ASCII tables (dst is a subsection 3.3.3.2.1.1 of the ccf section). Issue 5.1 defined 48: cur, lgf, grp, grpa and grpk were added in issue 6.0. Besides the tables, dynamic synthetic parameters are defined in one file per parameter (section 3.3.2.1.2); this project stores those files in the SQLite table 'synthetic(NAME, SOURCE)', which is not an ICD table.

notes.topic: non-ICD tables in the SQLite databases
notes.text: Tables present in the databases but not defined by any ICD issue: asw_sw_para, dup, pcf_glob_det, s13a, s13p, s13t (Solar Orbiter) and sw_para, ssy (SWA IDB). Their meaning is inferred from the data in the per-table JSON files.

The pyscos2000 schema (based on ICD issue 7.2, not available in this library) covers 36 of the 53 tables; it has no grp, grpa, grpk, dpf, dpc, gpf, gpc, spf, spc, ppf, ppc, cvs, cve, cvp, cps, pvs, psm. Naming differences: CPC_NAME (ICD 7.0: CPC_PNAME), CPC_OBTIP (CPC_OBTID), VDF_DOMAIN (VDF_DOMAINID), CSS_STATPTV (CSS_STAPTV). pyscos2000 adds PCF_DESCR2 as PCF field 24 and CPC_DESCR2 as CPC field 16 with CPC_ENDIAN moved to 17, whereas ICD 7.0 has CPC_ENDIAN as field 16. In the SQLite databases these 36 tables use pyscos2000 column names; the others use COL1..COLn.

In MIB__20250916M25925PFMS001_SOL every non-empty ICD table file has exactly the ICD 7.0 number of TAB-separated fields per line, except cpc.dat (15 fields: the 7.0 future-extension CPC_ENDIAN is absent, i.e. the 6.9 layout). Lines contain no CR characters and pcf.dat contains only 7-bit ASCII. Empty optional fields are present as consecutive TABs. Eleven ICD tables are delivered as empty (0-byte) files: cps, gpc, gpf, grpa, lgf, ppc, ppf, psm, pst, psv, pvs (pst/psv/pvs/psm/cps empty means no parameter sets are used). The 2020 release has the same layout (ptv.dat empty).

The SWA instrument database files follow an older layout: pcf.dat 19 fields, cpc.dat 13, caf.dat 7 and pic.dat 6 (no PIC_APID), consistent with ICD issues between 6.0 and 6.4, while ccf.dat already has 21 fields (CCF_SUBSCHEDID, from 6.0). Its vdf.dat contains 70 version records.

tables[].solo_2025_raw_fields_per_line gives the distribution of TAB-separated fields per line in the raw 2025 .dat file as '<fields>x<lines>' (e.g. '23x126745'). tables[].issues gives per-issue presence, PDF page and parsed field count. ptc_pfc_*[].print_style records how the Appendix A row is typeset (bold, italic, normal) and solo_pcf_count_2025 / solo_cpc_count_2025 count matching rows in pcf / cpc of MIB__20250916M25925PFMS001_SOL (for '>0' rows: all PFC values above 0).

In the SQLite databases, tables loaded from empty files and lacking a pyscos2000 schema get a single placeholder column COL1 (e.g. gpf, gpc, ppf, ppc, cps, pvs, psm, grpa, ssy); this does not reflect the ICD field count.

Annex 1 of 7.0 begins with 14 'document changes applicable to all evolution releases' (removal of partial import options, 'calibration definition' wording, limit on parameters in status-consistency checks, nested VPD repetitions, group repeaters in sequences, parameter views in CVE, removal of the circular-dependency constraint for synthetic parameters from R3.1, CSS_RELTIME/CSS_EXTIME formats, CDF_BIT usage, PID_EVID, SCR 2245, global FARM interlock, parameters for dynamic defaults/PTV/CEV, CDF_VALUE radix). The issue that introduced them is not stated.
No issue 6.8 appears in any change log. Issue 7.2 is not in this library; it is known only through pyscos2000's schema.

ICD 7.0 lists as applicable the SCOS-2000 Monitoring, Commanding and System Level SRDs, the TC Sequences definitions ICD (AD-4), the TM Displays and Printout definitions ICD (AD-5) and the System Control ADD (AD-6); references include ESA PSS-07-101 PUS issue 1 (RD-6), the Rosetta space/ground ICD (RD-7), CCSDS 301.0-B-2 time codes (RD-8), the Synthetic Parameters SUM (RD-9), Stack Import ICD (RD-12), the ESA packet telecommand standard issue 2.0, printed as 'ESA PSS-074-107' (RD-14), NIS/NCTRS ICD (RD-18), NIS Throw Events ICD (RD-19) and ECSS-E-70-41A (RD-20, to be replaced by ECSS-E-ST-70-41C).
